Package com.irurueta.authserver.authorization.api.web.social

Class FederatedUserMapper

java.lang.Object
com.irurueta.authserver.authorization.api.web.social.FederatedUserMapper
@Component public class FederatedUserMapper extends Object
Maps the user an external provider described onto the user the rest of the server sees: the principal of the session, whose name is the local account's username (so it is the sub of the issued tokens, as it is for every other way of signing in), whose authorities are the account's own, and which still carries the claims of the provider (the amr among them).

The principal is stored with the authorization and read back at the token request through a polymorphic allow-list, so every claim is normalised to a JSON-friendly value first: lists are mutable lists (an immutable one is not on the allow-list), instants are epoch seconds and URLs are strings.

    • toLocalUser

      public org.springframework.security.oauth2.core.user.OAuth2User toLocalUser(org.springframework.security.oauth2.core.user.OAuth2User upstream, Collection<String> kept, String email, String username, Collection<? extends org.springframework.security.core.GrantedAuthority> authorities)
      Maps an OAuth 2.0 user. Only the attributes in kept are carried over (the profile of such a provider may hold nested objects that have no business in the session).
      Parameters:
      upstream - the user the provider described.
      kept - names of the attributes to keep.
      email - verified e-mail address, or null; it replaces the provider's email.
      username - username of the local account.
      authorities - authorities of the local account.
      Returns:
      a user named after the account.

    • emailVerified

      public boolean emailVerified(org.springframework.security.oauth2.core.oidc.user.OidcUser user)
      Tells whether the provider vouches for the e-mail address of an OpenID Connect user. The standard email_verified claim does (a string "true" too, as Apple sends it); Microsoft Entra ID has no such claim in its default tokens, so its optional xms_edov claim counts, and without either the address is not verified: Entra's email can be set by a tenant administrator to any value.
      Parameters:
      user - the user the provider described.
      Returns:
      true when the address is verified.
